$comment: Scored tasks for the SvGrid MCP server. Deterministic and model-free on purpose: every task asserts what the SERVER returns for a given call, so it runs in CI for free and a ranking regression cannot hide. retrieval = did the right thing surface in the top hits. repair = given code a model would plausibly write from memory, does check + auto-fix reach clean. negative = there is no good answer; does the server say so instead of returning plausible noise.

tasks.query: how do I pin a column
how do I group rows by a column
how do I sort by two columns

tasks.$comment: The single most common way a model writes SvGrid from memory: with another grid's prop names.
tasks.source:
<script lang="ts">
  import { SvGrid } from '@svgrid/grid'
  const columns = [{ accessorKey: 'name', headerName: 'Name' }]
  const rows = [{ name: 'Ada' }]
</script>

<SvGrid rowData={rows} columnDefs={columns} enableSorting />

<script lang="ts">
  import { SvGrid } from '@svgrid/grid'
  const columns = [{ dataIndex: 'id', title: 'ID' }, { accessor: 'name', label: 'Name' }]
</script>

<SvGrid data={[]} columns={columns} />

<script lang="ts">
  import { SvGrid } from '@svgrid/grid'
  const columns = [{ valueGetter: (r) => r.name, cellRenderer: 'x' }]
</script>

<SvGrid rows={[]} columns={columns} enableFilter />
